title: Showcase, Assessment & Reflection
summary: Learners present their finished solution with two justified choices, complete a short Term-1 assessment sampling all four strands, and set a goal for next term.
objectives: Present the finished solution and explain at least two design/evaluation choices.
Demonstrate the term's key outcomes in a short assessment task.
State one thing learned and set one goal for next term.

body: This is your moment to show what you built and what you learned. You will present your finished solution, explain the choices behind it, complete a short assessment, and set a goal to grow even more next term.

sections.heading: I can…
items: I can present my finished solution and explain at least two design or evaluation choices.
I can show the term's key outcomes in a short assessment task.
I can state one thing I learned and set one goal for next term.

terms.definition: A short, clear explanation of your solution and its value.
To give the reason and evidence behind a choice.
A task that shows what you have learned across the strands.
Thinking about what worked and what you would do next.
A clear target for your next step of learning.

sections.heading: A pitch that tells the truth
body: A strong [[pitch]] names your user, the problem, how your solution works, and the evidence that it is accurate, useful and safe.
Explain two choices by giving reasons, not just descriptions. Be honest about one limit. Honesty makes your work more trustworthy, not weaker.

sections.heading: Show the whole term, then look ahead
body: The short [[assessment]] lets you show all four strands: understanding, building, evaluating and using responsibly, and wider effects.
Finish by naming one thing you learned and setting a [[goal]] for next term, aiming toward the Proficient tier.

sections.heading: Let's try it - hands-on
body: Complete the short assessment, then present your solution and justify two choices before setting your next-term goal.
items: Set out your evidence from the term.
Complete the short assessment task on your own.
Prepare a 60-second pitch with two justified choices.
Present to your group and answer one 'why' question.

sections.heading: Think about it
items: Which of your two choices are you proudest of, and why?
What limit of your solution is important to be honest about?

sections.heading: My reflection
items: Write one thing you learned this term.
Set one goal for Term 2 that moves you toward Proficient.

questions.prompt: In your pitch you have to justify a choice, not just describe it. Which sentence justifies the choice?

options.text: My sorter uses five rules — one each for plastic, paper, metal, glass and food waste.
I used a rule-based sorter because recycling categories have fixed correct answers, so the rules give the same reliable result every time.
I used a rule-based sorter because my group voted for that one.
My sorter was finished on time and looks clear on the screen.

feedback.correct: A justified choice gives the reason behind it — fixed correct answers suit fixed rules — rather than listing what the solution contains.
feedback.incorrect: Listing the rules, reporting a vote or praising the look all describe the solution; a justification says why that choice suited the problem.

questions.prompt: Your Term-1 assessment has to show all four strands. Match each piece of evidence to the strand it shows.

left.text: I can explain how a system that follows written rules is different from one that learns from examples.
I made a working prototype that takes an item and puts it into a category.
I ran my solution on six items whose correct answers I already knew, and recorded how many it got right.
I described who might be treated unfairly if the whole school used my solution.

feedback.correct: Each strand needs its own evidence: explaining shows concepts, making shows design and build, testing shows evaluation, and thinking about users shows wider effects.
feedback.incorrect: Ask what each piece of evidence proves you can do — explain, build, test or think about who is affected — and the strand follows from that.

questions.prompt: Which of these belong in a 60-second pitch that tells the truth? Select all that apply.

options.text: Name your user and the problem your solution solves.
Give the evidence that your results were accurate.
State one honest limit of your solution.
Promise that your solution never gets anything wrong, so nobody doubts it.
Describe your two choices without saying why you made them.

feedback.correct: A truthful pitch names the user and problem, backs its claims with evidence, and is open about one limit.
feedback.incorrect: Promising perfection is not evidence, and a choice with no reason is only a description — neither makes a pitch more convincing.

questions.prompt: Admitting one limit of your solution during your pitch makes your work less trustworthy.

feedback.correct: Correct — honesty about a limit makes your work more trustworthy, because your audience can believe the claims you do make.
feedback.incorrect: The lesson says the opposite: being honest about a limit strengthens your pitch rather than weakening it.

questions.prompt: Put the showcase and assessment steps into the order that makes each step possible.

items.text: Set out your evidence from the term.
Complete the short assessment task on your own.
Prepare a 60-second pitch with two justified choices.
Present to your group and answer one 'why' question.
Write one thing you learned and one goal for Term 2.

feedback.correct: Evidence first so you can draw on it, the assessment on your own before you hear other people's ideas, then prepare, present, and reflect once you know how it went.
feedback.incorrect: Each step feeds the next: you need your evidence out before you can use it, and you can only reflect on your learning after you have presented.

formative.targets: Summative Term-1 task samples all four strands at Emerging; reflection informs Term 2
formative.check: Short Term-1 performance task marked with the analytic rubric + structured self-reflection
formative.successCriteria: Demonstrates each strand at Emerging; articulates two justified design/evaluation choices.
formative.evidence: Assessed task + reflection; results reported per strand.
